name: NVIDIA DGX H100 / H200 system: 10.2 kW max air-cooled 8-GPU node (6x 3.3 kW PSU, 4+2 redundant)
notes: THE CONTROL CASE, AND THE REASON H100-CLASS INFERENCE IS STILL DEPLOYABLE WHERE GB200-CLASS IS NOT. Every figure from the vendor's own DGX H100/H200 User Guide. POWER: 6 x 3.3 kW power supplies, 3300 W at 200-240 V / 16 A each, configured 4+2 redundant, with the table headed '10.2 kW max.' for the system. Installed PSU capacity is 6 x 3.3 = 19.8 kW against a 10.2 kW max system draw. THERMAL AND AIRFLOW, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AIR-COOLABLE AT ALL: heat output 38,557 BTU/hr, airflow 1105 CFM front-to-back at 80% fan PWM, operating temperature 5-30 C, relative humidity 20-80% non-condensing. That 1105 CFM figure is the real procurement gate - it is a loud, airflow-hungry 8U box (287.6 lbs / 130.45 kg, 35.3 in deep), and the room must move that much air past it. Compare to GB200 NVL72's liquid-loop rack with fans only on the non-compute components. PSU FAILURE BEHAVIOUR, VERBATIM AND OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT: 'If three PSUs lose power as a result of a data center issue or power distribution unit failure, the system continues to function, but at a reduced performance level.' Also: the system only boots if at least three PSUs are operational; below three only the BMC is available; 'Do not operate the system with PSUs depopulated.' So a single PDU or PSU-distribution failure degrades the node rather than crashing it - good for uptime, but the degraded state is silent and will show up as reduced throughput rather than as an alert in most monitoring setups. That is recorded separately as gotchas/dgx-psu-depop-silent-degraded-throughput. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE AI-INFERENCE BUYER: 10.2 kW per node sits just above Vantage's published colo standard of 8.3 kW/rack average (projecting 11 kW+ in the near future) and comfortably below their 20 kW air-cooled ceiling. A standard colo data module can host a DGX-class node today with no facility work. A GB200 NVL72 rack cannot be placed in the same room without liquid infrastructure, different power shelves and a different busbar. This is the cleanest boundary in the whole power-density picture: below ~20 kW/rack air cooling is a solved procurement problem; above it you are buying a facility, not a server.
